title: Recording with the original kept
description: Telling the source audio, the working version and a separate copy apart, and seeing the saved state of each file.

blocks.text: A person has finished an important recording and wants to be sure they will be able to open it later. The app tells the source file, the processed version and the exported copy apart; it shows where each of them is available.

quote.text: One year of calls pertinent to my ongoing legal case are nowhere to be found, though my iCloud still shows 2gb of data stored for this app.

blocks.text: The first scenario is to record, rename, close the app and play the file again, then open a separate copy outside it. A failed transfer must not delete the only saved recording.

This is first of all a requirement for a voice recorder’s reliability. A file being safe does not guarantee that the circumstances of the recording were safe, or that the material is fit for someone else’s decision; a standalone product needs a more definite job than a general promise of protection.
